panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Panel (a) is clinical photo of back in 12-year-old boy with actinic prurigo showing erythematous excoriated papules as captioned. b: Panel (b) is clinical photo of arm in same 12-year-old boy with actinic prurigo showing erythematous excoriated papules as captioned.
panels.attribution_text: Morissette and Coulombe. Refractory pediatric actinic prurigo successfully treated with upadacitinib: A case report.. SAGE open medical case reports 2025. doi:10.1177/2050313x251341558. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Actinic prurigo skin lesions. Erythematous and excoriated papules on back (a) and arm (b) in a 12-year-old boy affected by actinic prurigo after a shirtless sunny day.
in_text_mentions: The patient was known for herpes labialis, IgA and C2 deficiencies. He developed pruritic papules on his face, neck, trunk and extremities during summertime (see Figure 1). On examination, subtle cheilitis and conjunctivitis were noted. Systemic symptoms were absent. A complete workup to rule out photodermatoses revealed antinuclear antibody 1/320, elevated ds-DNA at 910 UI/mL and normal C3, C4, ENA and porphyrin levels. Multiple skin biopsies showed subacute spongiotic dermatitis with a negative lupus band test. Pediatric rheumatology was consulted, and a diagnosis of lupus was excluded. Gene

findings.evidence: Caption: 'Histopathological features of actinic prurigo cheilitis'; in-text: 'AP cheilitis exhibits acanthosis with spongiosis and vacuolation of the basal cell layer overlying a dense lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate that forms well-defined lymphoid follicles'.

panels.rationale: Single H&E histology panel from an open-access article titled on actinic prurigo cheilitis; the caption and in-text explicitly attribute the histopathology to AP cheilitis. The image shows the described features: squamous epithelium with spongiosis overlying a dense lymphoid infiltrate forming a well-defined lymphoid follicle, matching the in-text description of AP cheilitis histology. Real patient tissue, not a diagram/chart/control; no third-party copyright indicated. Skin tone not assessable from histology, so null. [raw subtype: cheilitis]
panels.attribution_text: Cedeño-Suárez et al. Value of the toluidine blue test as an aid to determine the biopsy site in actinic prurigo cheilitis.. Autopsy & case reports 2021. doi:10.4322/acr.2021.247. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological features of actinic prurigo cheilitis.
in_text_mentions: Histologically, AP cheilitis exhibits acanthosis with spongiosis and vacuolation of the basal cell layer overlying a dense lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate that forms well-defined lymphoid follicles (comprising B lymphocytes in the center and T lymphocytes at the periphery), macrophages, eosinophils, and mast cells (Figure 1).2

panels.attribution_text: Cedeño-Suárez et al. Value of the toluidine blue test as an aid to determine the biopsy site in actinic prurigo cheilitis.. Autopsy & case reports 2021. doi:10.4322/acr.2021.247. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: A – Clinical aspects of actinic prurigo cheilitis; B – Persistent staining with toluidine blue after removing dye with 2% acetic acid (positive zone).
in_text_mentions: We included 20 patients (11 women and 9 men) aged between 7 and 45 years (mean 25.7) who presented clinically with AP cheilitis (Figure 2A). The detection technique comprised the application of toluidine blue with a swab along the affected vermillion border. After 60 seconds, the site was cleaned with 2% acetic acid solution and rinsed with water or saline solution, leaving clearly defined an area in which the dye persisted visible in the tissue (Figure 2B).

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: 'Nuclear positivity in basal layer of p53 in AP cheilitis and skin lesions. In cheilitis, the positivity was in the perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate.'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Immunohistochemistry panel explicitly captioned as actinic prurigo (AP) cheilitis; shows p53 nuclear positivity in the basal layer with a dense perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate in the lip mucosa, matching the article's focus on apoptosis markers in actinic prurigo. Disease attribution is clear from the caption and article title. B: Companion IHC panel explicitly captioned as actinic prurigo skin lesions; shows p53 nuclear positivity in the basal layer of the epidermis. Caption specifies only 'skin lesions' without a lesion subtype, so no vocabulary skin finding is asserted; the visible IHC pattern is recorded as a proposed finding. Disease attribution is supported by the caption and the article title on actinic prurigo immunohistochemistry.
panels.attribution_text: Cuevas-González et al. Apoptosis and apoptotic pathway in actinic prurigo by immunohistochemistry.. Medicina oral, patologia oral y cirugia bucal 2016. doi:10.4317/medoral.20765. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: A and B. (400x) Nuclear positivity in basal layer of p53 in AP cheilitis and skin lesions. In cheilitis, the positivity was in the perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate.
in_text_mentions: Of the skin lesions, p53 and caspase 3 were expressed in 18 of 24 cases (75%), and 13 were positive for Bcl-2 (54%). None was positive for Bax or Fas. (Figs. 2,3).
